scalePanel.howScaleWorksBody: {{brand}} reads the rendered resolution of your PDF automatically. You only need to pick the architectural scale that matches what's printed on the blueprint's title block (usually bottom right corner, e.g. 1/4" = 1'). If your scale is non-standard, or the drawing was scanned and resized, use Manual Calibration: click Manual from the dropdown, draw a line along a dimension you know (like a wall labeled 10'-0"), and enter the actual length.

scalePanel.aiHint: AI reads your blueprint title block and sets the scale automatically.
scalePanel.aiLocked: 🔒 AI Scale Detection — available on Plus plan
scalePanel.helpManualText: Find any printed dimension on the drawing (e.g. a wall labeled 24'-0"). Enter that distance, click <1>Set Calibration Line</1>, then click both endpoints of that dimension on the blueprint. Scale is set exactly.
scalePanel.helpAiText: Click <1>AI Detect Scale</1> above. AI reads the title block and applies the scale. Verified automatically with a dimension check.
scalePanel.helpDropdownText: Pick the scale stated on the drawing from the dropdown above. The system checks automatically that the resulting dimensions are reasonable.
scalePanel.helpTip: Tip: For residential blueprints, 1/4 inch = 1 foot is the most common scale.

draw.hintCount: Click each item on the blueprint to count it.
draw.hintLine: Click to trace the line. Double-click or Finish to close.
draw.hintPolygon: Click to draw polygon corners. Double-click or Finish to close.
draw.ceilingTypeTip: Vaulted = symmetric slopes meeting at a center peak. Tray = recessed center with vertical edges. Shed = single low-to-high slope. Pick the type that matches the room.
draw.pitchTip: Roof pitch describes the steepness as rise over run. A pitch of 8/12 means the roof rises 8 inches for every 12 inches of horizontal distance. Common residential pitches: 4/12 (low slope), 6/12 (medium), 8/12 (medium-steep), 10/12 (steep — most common for vaulted ceilings), 12/12 (very steep, 45°).
draw.wallHeightTip: The actual height of the wall from floor to ceiling, in feet. Standard residential is 8-9 ft. Commercial spaces are typically 10-12 ft.
draw.doorTip: Subtracts standard door area (21 SF) from wall surface. Standard door = 7' tall x 3' wide.
draw.windowTip: Subtracts standard window area (15 SF) from wall surface. Click + Custom for exact dimensions.
draw.customTip: Add a custom opening (large window, archway, fireplace) by entering exact width and height.

tips.tip1: Drop multiple PDFs at once on a job page to add them as separate blueprints.
tips.tip2: Splitting large PDFs into manageable chunks keeps things fast — try the Split feature on any 100+ page blueprint.
tips.tip3: Inline-rename a blueprint by clicking its name on the Job Overview page.
tips.tip4: Use the timeline scrubber to compare measurements across blueprints in the same job.
tips.tip5: Need help? Click feedback in the user menu — every message reaches us directly.
tips.tip6: Set your default trade categories once in Settings and they'll apply to every new job.
tips.tip7: Press Escape from any modal to close it — keyboard shortcuts make repetitive work fast.
tips.tip8: Your storage allowance is in the user menu — keep an eye on it as your blueprint library grows.
tips.tip9: Import your whole client list from a spreadsheet — upload a CSV or Excel file and let RivetDog map the columns for you.
tips.tip10: Not every job needs a blueprint — start a new job and choose Enter Measurements Manually to quote on the spot.
tips.tip11: Send one estimate with Good, Better, and Best pricing — tiered quotes help clients say yes to more.
tips.tip12: Use a Lump Sum line item for flat-rate work like permits or trip fees — no quantity math needed.
tips.tip13: Filter your Time page by any date range — pick a preset or set custom From and To dates for exactly the period you need.
tips.tip14: Job Costing shows estimated vs actual margin per job, so you know which work actually makes you money.
tips.tip15: Send each crew member a Pay Statement PDF — job-by-job hours and pay, ready to hand off.
tips.tip16: Log expenses against a job as you go — materials, labor, and overhead all roll into your real profit.
tips.tip17: Upload your logo once and it brands every estimate, invoice, and client portal automatically.
tips.tip18: Clients can accept or decline an estimate right from their portal — no phone tag required.
tips.tip19: Track collected vs billed on every invoice so you always know what is still outstanding.
tips.tip20: Pricing a big job? Save your common line items to the pricing library and reuse them on every estimate.
tips.tip21: A dog's sense of smell is up to 100,000 times sharper than yours — they can practically sniff out a fresh coat of paint.
tips.tip22: Dogs dream just like people do — puppies and senior dogs tend to dream the most.
tips.tip23: A wagging tail is not always a happy one — the direction and speed actually change what your dog is saying.
tips.tip24: The old rule that one dog year equals seven human years is a myth — the first year alone counts for about fifteen.
tips.tip25: Rotate the treats you use as rewards — dogs, like contractors, work harder when the payoff keeps them guessing.
tips.tip26: Ten minutes of play can tire a dog out more than a long walk — a good sniff-and-fetch session works the brain and the body.
tips.tip27: Why did the painter bring a dog to the job site? For a second opinion on the coat.
tips.tip28: What do you call a dog who can measure a whole house? A rule-triever.
